battle.name: 秦滅韓之戰
battle.brief: 西元前230年，秦王政命內史騰率軍自關中沿洛河谷東出，攻韓都新鄭。韓王安舉國之兵抵抗而節節失利，各城相繼降秦，遂遣使請和，韓國成為六國中最先被滅者。卡面的斯巴達長矛並未出現在韓地戰場，但同時代秦軍的長矛、車兵與弩機，正是把韓軍逼入絕境的骨架。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 西元前230年開打的一場戰爭，正式交戰的雙方只有秦國與韓國，但戰局的真正範圍是整個東周晚期的中原。韓國是當時六國中疆域最小、兵力最弱的一個：從西元前453年鄭國滅亡起算，韓失去大片封地，到滅國前只剩下新鄭、宜陽、陽翟、黃池、上蔡、故城等數處據點，領土被秦、魏、楚三面夾住，向北不過一日行程便到魏國河內與秦國控制的三川之野，向南是楚國的方城與潁川，向東是魏國的大梁與陳留。這種地形意味著韓沒有縱深可以調度，也沒有可以退守的第二座深城。韓國的軍隊以都城的宿衛與郡縣的常備兵為主，郡縣徵發的卒伍、韓王直屬的近衛，加上弓弩手與車兵，規模遠不足以與秦國的野戰主力相抗。韓也不是完全孤立：楚、魏、趙三國在名義上都是韓的盟國，前230年前後它們自身正被秦軍的另外兩條戰線牽制，韓求援而不得應。雙方的指揮系統則完全不同：秦王政以相邦、將軍與各郡守構成中央與戰區的雙重架構，出兵時由主將率領大軍，郡縣負責徵發、輸糧與築道；韓王安事實上只有都城一處可以調度的地方。整場戰爭的樣貌，就是秦國這套可以縱深用兵的國家機器，對上韓國一個幾乎只剩一座都城的政權。
countriesEn: The war that opened in 230 BC had only two formal belligerents, Qin and Han, but the real extent of the contest was the whole of the late Eastern Zhou central plain. Han was at that moment the smallest and weakest of the six states: counting from the fall of Zheng in 453 BC, Han had lost most of its old fiefs, and by the eve of its destruction it held only a handful of sites such as Xinzheng, Yiyang, Yangdi, Huangchi, Shangcai and Gucheng, its territory pinched between Qin on the west, Wei to the north and east, and Chu to the south. To the north a single day's march carried the army to the Wei commandery of Henei and to the San River country already controlled by Qin; to the south lay the Fangcheng of Chu and the Ying valley; to the east lay Wei's Daliang and Chenliu. Such a geography meant that Han had no depth to manoeuvre in and no second deep city to fall back to. The Han army consisted chiefly of the garrison of the capital and the standing troops of its commanderies, the levies raised by the counties, the royal guard close to the king, together with crossbowmen and chariotry; it was far too small to stand against the field armies of Qin. Nor was Han entirely alone: Chu, Wei and Zhao were all its allies in name, but around 230 BC they were themselves pinned down by other Qin fronts, and Han's appeals for help went unanswered. The two command systems were nothing alike. Under King Zheng of Qin, the chancellor, the generals and the commandery governors formed a two-level structure of central and theatre command: a main general led the field army, while the counties handled the levies, the transport of grain and the building of roads. King An of Han, by contrast, effectively had only the capital to draw on. The whole shape of the war was that Qin state machinery, capable of fighting in depth, set against a Han government that had been reduced to a single city.
people: 這場戰爭留得下名字的人不多，但每一位都站在關鍵位置上。韓國的國君是韓王安，韓桓惠王的兒子，在位不過十來年，國勢在他手上已跌到谷底；史書寫到他時的語氣，是一個被臣下與強鄰共同推著走的國君，最後的動作是請降。秦王政是這場戰役的推手，他西元前247年即位時年僅十三歲，到前230年剛過二十一歲，滅韓是他親自排定的次序中的第一步，也是他在位期間第一次親手拆掉一個國家。執行者是秦將內史騰，內史是秦國掌管郡縣民政與軍賦的官職，騰以秦軍主將的身分率兵東出，滅韓有功。同一時期秦軍在北面還有另一支大軍，桓齮（後來逃亡燕國、又為荊軻所取其首級的那位將領）正率兵攻趙，前後取河間、太原、上黨，兩條戰線一東一北，把韓夾在中間。工程與謀略方面還有兩個名字：鄭國是韓國派到秦國來修渠的水利工程師，他主持的鄭國渠從西元前246年開鑿，名義上替秦國的農田引水灌溉，實則要拖住秦國東出的腳步；工程開成之後，秦王政並沒有殺他，還說渠成則秦國富強。蘇秦則是合縱的說客，他在《史記·蘇秦列傳》裡縱論六國的存亡，韓國的處境是他著墨最多的地方之一，而韓王的取捨最終沒有採納縱的一途。往後的秦將王翦與王賁，接連滅掉趙、魏、楚、燕、齊，把韓亡國之後的次序做完；韓王安降秦後被封為通武君，遷居秦地，數年後因子孫謀反被誅，其時已在秦律之下。
peopleEn: Few people in this war can be named, but each of them stood in a decisive position. The ruler of Han was King An of Han, son of King Huanhui of Han, whose reign lasted barely a decade and during which the state fell to its lowest point; the tone of the historians who write of him is that of a king pushed along by his ministers and his powerful neighbours, and his last act was to sue for peace. King Zheng of Qin was the man who drove the campaign. He had come to the throne in 247 BC at the age of thirteen, and in 230 BC he had just passed his twenty-first year; the destruction of Han was the first step of a sequence he had personally laid out, and the first state he personally took apart during his reign. The man who carried it out was the Qin general Neishi Teng, the neishi being the Qin office that administered the civil and military levies of the commanderies and counties; Teng led the army eastward as commander of the Qin forces and was rewarded for the fall of Han. At the same time Qin had a second army in the north, where Huan Yi, the general who later fled to Yan and from whose head Jing Ke took a trophy, was campaigning against Zhao and had taken Hanjian, Taiyuan and Shangdang; one front to the east and one to the north enclosed Han between them. Two further names belong to works and to strategy. Zheng Guo was the hydraulic engineer whom Han sent to Qin to dig a canal: the Zhengguo Canal, begun in 246 BC, was in form an irrigation work for the Qin fields and in truth a device to hold up Qin's departure eastward; when the works were finished King Zheng did not put him to death, remarking that with the canal completed Qin would be strong. Su Qin was the advocate of the vertical alliance, and in the biography of Su Qin in the Records of the Grand Historian he surveyed the survival of the six states at length, the position of Han among them occupying some of his fullest pages, while the choice King An actually made never followed the line of union. The Qin generals Wang Jian and Wang Ben later destroyed Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi in turn, completing the sequence that began with the fall of Han. King An of Han, after surrendering, was given the title Lord of Tongwu and resettled in Qin territory; several years later he was put to death with his descendants for conspiracy, by which time he stood already under Qin law.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是斯巴達長矛，也就是 dory：西元前八世紀以來希臘世界通用的刺擊長矛，木桿約兩公尺，前端裝鐵或青銅的矛頭，槍尾留一段金屬套或尖錐，以便插地支撐。卡面那句話說，方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住，這句話在秦滅韓的戰場上要改寫一次：長矛確實是那一代重裝步兵的骨幹，但秦軍在接觸之前就已經決定勝負，靠的不是矛，是弩的齊射與車兵的衝撞。斯巴達長矛本身沒有出現在韓地戰場上，這一點不必含糊；它的價值在於提供了一個同時代的對照。西元前三世紀的地中海與東亞，重裝步兵同樣靠一件兩公尺上下的長柄刺擊武器撐住密集隊形，秦軍的對應物是通長約三公尺的直刃矛，韓軍與楚軍所用的長戈。東亞的長柄兵器分工比希臘式更細：矛負責直刺，戈負責鉤啄與撕扯，兩者配合近身；斯巴達長矛把這兩件事都交給同一件兵器，秦軍則用札甲、大盾與密集的箭石覆蓋正面，戈矛從盾牆的縫隙中伸出。秦軍的裝備體系還包括銅製機弩（秦始皇陵陪葬坑出土的秦弩與成束箭鏃，是秦軍遠射能力的實物證據）、柳葉形刃的秦劍、長援的戈、皮甲與金屬札甲、青銅頭盔，以及御用馬匹與車乘，史記提到的駃騠與林胡之馬即出現在秦的車騎之中。攻城方面，秦軍備有雲梯、撞車、填壕的土木器材與封鎖打援的手段；後勤靠牛車輸送糧秣，沿途設亭傳驛站。韓方則以弓弩見長，韓國的冶鐵與弩機製作在列國中素有名聲，宜陽一帶的鐵更是韓國最後的資源底子。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card face is the Spartan spear, the dory: the thrusting spear used throughout the Greek world from the eighth century BC onward, a wooden shaft about two metres long with an iron or bronze head at the front and a metal sleeve or spike left at the butt so that it could be planted in the ground to steady a push. The sentence on the card says that in the phalanx it is the spear, not the sword, that first decides who can hold the ground; on the field of Qin's destruction of Han that sentence has to be rewritten once. The long spear was indeed the backbone of the heavy infantry of that generation, but the Qin army decided the issue before contact was made, and not with the spear: it was decided by the volley of the crossbow and the charge of the chariots. The Spartan spear itself never appeared on the battlefield of Han, and there is no need to be vague about that; its value lies in providing a same-period comparison. In the Mediterranean and in East Asia alike in the third century BC, the heavy infantry depended on a thrusting weapon of about two metres to hold a dense formation together; the Qin counterpart was the straight-bladed spear of a full length of roughly three metres, and the long dagger-axe used by the troops of Han and Chu. The East Asian long-hafted weapons were divided more finely than the Greek type: the spear for the direct thrust, the dagger-axe for hooking and tearing, the two working together at close quarters. The Spartan dory assigned both jobs to a single weapon; the Qin infantry instead covered the front with lamellar armour, large shields and a dense volume of arrows and stones, and drove the spear and the dagger-axe through the gaps of the shield wall. The Qin equipment system further included bronze trigger mechanisms for crossbows, the Qin crossbows and bundled arrowheads excavated from the accessory pits of the First Emperor's mausoleum being the physical evidence of the army's shooting power; Qin swords with a leaf-shaped blade; dagger-axes with long blades; leather and metal lamellar armour; bronze helmets; and the horses and draught animals of the chariots and the transport, the tuotuo and the Linhu breed named in the Records of the Grand Historian all appearing in Qin's teams. For siege work the Qin army brought scaling ladders, rams, timber and earth for filling ditches, and the means of sealing roads and cutting off relief; on the logistics side, grain and fodder were moved on ox carts, with post stations and relay stations set along the route. The Han side was known for its bows and crossbows; Han ironworking and the manufacture of crossbow mechanisms had a standing among the states, and the iron of the Yiyang district was the last resource base left to Han.
tactics: 秦軍在這場戰役裡的打法可以拆成三段。第一段是接觸前的投射：弩手與弓手在遠處以齊射覆蓋韓軍的隊形與城頭，壓制守軍的射擊與指揮。第二段是車兵衝撞：秦軍以數百乘戎車在窄道上展開，一個車組三人作戰，一人御車、兩人持戈矛，車輪壓住地面障礙，盾車在前掩護，衝散韓軍的陣線。第三段才是步兵接戰，長矛與戈從盾後伸出，把被車兵和弩箭打亂的守軍逐段吃掉。這套次序與希臘方陣「以盾牆與長矛正面推壓」的做法不同：秦軍把勝負的決定點前移到遠射與車衝兩步，而不是交上手的那一刻。攻城方面，秦軍對韓國城邑用的是封鎖加強攻：先以弩兵與游騎切斷韓城與外界的聯絡，斷其糧道與援兵，再集中車兵與步卒攻城，圍城打援，同時用填壕、築壘、雲梯與穿地等手段削弱城防。韓軍的戰術選擇其實不多：韓國可用的野戰兵少，只能依托宜陽、成皋一線的關隘與洛陽南面的山道節節抵抗，試圖把秦軍拖進攻城消耗；可惜韓境內沒有足以遲滯秦軍的深山大澤，韓的城邑多為平原上的小城，缺少可以固守的地形骨架，一旦被圍而外援不至，就只剩死守與突圍兩個選項。季節與河流也影響全線：秋天是洛水與伊洛河最可用的運糧時段，冬季河面結冰、行軍受限，春汛則使渡河與築壘變難。整體而言，這是一場以國家總力碾壓一國最後據點的戰爭，戰術空間被國家結構壓得很窄。
tacticsEn: The Qin method in this campaign can be broken into three stages. The first is the projection of fire before contact: crossbowmen and archers blanketed the Han formations and the tops of the Han walls from a distance, suppressing the shooting and the command of the defenders. The second is the impact of the chariots: the Qin army deployed several hundred war chariots along the narrow roads, a team of three men to each vehicle, one driving and two armed with dagger-axe and spear, the wheels grinding over the obstacles of the ground and shield-bearing vehicles moving in front as cover, shattering the Han line. The third stage is the infantry engagement, the long spears and dagger-axes reaching out from behind the shields to cut down the defenders in sections, already disordered by the chariots and the bolts. This sequence differs from the Greek phalanx, which pressed forward with shield wall and spear in a single continuous push; the Qin army moved the decisive point of the battle two steps further back, to the shooting and the chariot charge, rather than to the moment of hand-to-hand fighting. Against the Han cities Qin combined blockade with assault: crossbowmen and roving cavalry first cut the cities off from the outside world, severing their grain roads and their relief, then the chariots and foot were concentrated on the siege, with relief columns intercepted on the way in, while ditches were filled, works thrown up, and scaling ladders and mining used to work at the defences. Han's tactical options were in fact very few. With so few troops available for field operations, Han could only rely on the passes along Yiyang and Chenggao and on the roads south of Luoyang to resist step by step, in the hope of dragging the Qin army into a grinding siege; but there was no deep mountain or great marsh within Han's borders to slow the Qin army down, and Han's cities were mostly small towns on the open plain, lacking the terrain skeleton of a strong defence. Once encircled and unrelieved, only two choices remained: hold, or break out. Season and rivers shaped the line as well: autumn was the most usable season for moving grain along the Luo and the Yi and Luo rivers, in winter the ice on the water slowed marching, and in the spring floods made river crossings and the raising of works harder. Overall this was a war in which the total strength of a state was rolled over the last strongpoints of another, and the tactical space was crushed narrow by the structure of the two states.
data: 可以核對的數字不多，幾個節點卻站得住。時間：戰爭在西元前230年之內完成，從秦軍出兵到韓王安乞降，歷時不足一年；史書只記年份不載月日，戰役欄所標的月份沒有史據可依。距離：秦都咸陽到前線洛陽約四百餘公里，由洛陽沿洛水東南到韓都新鄭約一百五十公里，韓國全部領土的縱深不足一日行程。疆域：韓亡國時實際控制的面積約一萬平方公里上下，學界對當時人口的估計在百萬量級；秦在同一時期的版圖是韓的數百倍。軍隊：商鞅變法之後秦國以「兵車千乘」為編制基準，戰車一乘以三人作戰、一人御車，步兵則五人為伍、十人為什、五十人為屯、百人為百將、五百人為五百主，再上則為將；蘇秦對秦國的估計是「秦兵百萬、卒號百萬、飛車千乘、良馬萬匹」，這是謀士的誇大說法，只能當作量級參考，不能當作點名冊。兵器尺度：秦劍一般長六七十公分，最長的實物超過九十公分；秦矛通長多在三公尺上下；弩機為銅質，弩身連臂逾一公尺，射程一般估在二百公尺上下；箭桿約七十多公分；秦國戎車的車軛寬約一公尺半。損失：這場戰役沒有留下可核的陣亡數字，韓軍各城相繼投降與潰散，並無大軍被全殲於野外的記載；倒是此前數年秦伐韓的戰果，舊籍曾記斬首八萬之數，年代與數字各書互有出入，只宜當作前例的量級。財政與糧秣：秦以關中為根本，涇渭平原的餘糧經渭水、黃河、洛水一路東輸，郡縣負責徵發與築道，這是秦能連續遠征的底子。
dataEn: Few numbers can be checked, but several fixed points hold. Time: the war was completed within the year 230 BC, and less than a year passed from the departure of the Qin army to the surrender offer of King An of Han; the historians record only the year and give no month or day, so the month entered in the campaign field has no historical warrant. Distances: it is a little over four hundred kilometres from the Qin capital of Xianyang to the forward base at Luoyang, and about a hundred and fifty kilometres from Luoyang along the Luo river southeast to the Han capital of Xinzheng, while the whole depth of Han's territory was less than a single day's march. Territory: the area actually under Han control at its fall was on the order of ten thousand square kilometres, and scholarly estimates put the population at that time in the region of a million; the territory of Qin in the same years was hundreds of times larger. Armies: after the reforms of Shang Yang the Qin state used a thousand war chariots as the base of its establishment, each vehicle fought by three men with a fourth driving, while the infantry were organised in groups of five, ten, fifty, a hundred and five hundred, above which came the commanders; Su Qin's estimate of Qin, a hundred thousand troops called a million, a thousand flying chariots and ten thousand fine horses, is the exaggeration of a counsellor and can serve only as an order of magnitude, not as a roll of names. Scale of the arms: Qin swords generally ran to sixty or seventy centimetres, the longest surviving example exceeding ninety; Qin spears were often about three metres in full length; the crossbow mechanisms were of bronze with the bow and stock exceeding a metre, and the effective range is usually estimated at around two hundred metres; arrow shafts ran to a little over seventy centimetres; and the track width of the Qin war chariot was about a metre and a half. Losses: no verifiable casualty figure survives from this campaign, the Han garrisons surrendering or scattering city by city with no record of a field army annihilated in one battle; the results of Qin campaigns against Han in the preceding years are elsewhere recorded as eight thousand beheaded, though the dates and the figures differ from book to book and are useful only as a precedent for scale. On finance and supply: Qin rested on the Guanzhong base, the surplus of the Jing and Wei plains travelling east by way of the Wei, the Yellow and Luo rivers, with the counties responsible for levies and road building; that was the foundation on which Qin could campaign year after year.
cause: 為什麼會打起來，理由分四層。第一層是秦的戰略次序：范雎在《史記·范雎蔡澤列傳》裡留下的那句話是「遠交而近攻」，秦國對鄰近的韓魏用兵，對遠方的趙燕齊先行結好，於是離關中最近、國力最弱的韓成了第一個目標。前230年前後，秦軍在北面已由桓齮取趙的河間、太原、上黨，韓正被兩條戰線夾在中間。第二層是韓的地理死局：韓的疆域被秦、魏、楚三面包圍，新鄭、宜陽、成皋、陽翟串成的防線總長有限，沒有縱深可以換取時間，也沒有可以固守的山地骨架，北方的強鄰與南方的楚國，援軍都指望不上。第三層是韓國自身的凋敝：桓惠王以後，韓廷先後以土地、糧食與關市權益向秦國抵押求貸，兵役與賦斂越收越少，郡縣的守備只剩象征性的數目；韓王安當政時，朝中與秦方的私下往來也屢見於史筆。外交上同樣沒有出路：蘇秦縱論六國之勢、勸韓與諸國結縱，韓王沒有採納；韓國又曾想藉秦國的力量去對付趙國，在《史記·蘇秦列傳》的敘述裡，這反而替秦國多添了一個名分與一條通道。第四層是秦國的準備：商鞅留下的耕戰體制把關中的糧食剩餘變成了可以連年遠征的軍糧，郡縣的徵發、驛傳的接力與沿途的築道，使大軍不必就地取糧；兵器方面，秦有自成一格的弩機與箭桿作坊，也吸收了韓、楚一帶的冶鐵與弩術。鄭國渠則是韓國拖延的最後一著，結果是秦國的糧田又多了一片。
causeEn: Why the fighting began can be read in four layers. The first is the strategic sequence of Qin: the sentence left by Fan Ju in the biography of Fan Ju and Cai Ze in the Records of the Grand Historian is to make alliances with the distant and attack the near, and so Qin fought its neighbours Han and Wei while first coming to terms with distant Zhao, Yan and Qi; the state nearest to Guanzhong and weakest in itself, Han, therefore became the first target. Around 230 BC the Qin army in the north had already taken Hanjian, Taiyuan and Shangdang in Zhao under Huan Yi, and Han lay between the two fronts. The second layer is the geographical deadlock of Han: its territory was surrounded by Qin, Wei and Chu, and the line strung out through Xinzheng, Yiyang, Chenggao and Yangdi was short, with no depth in which to buy time and no mountainous frame on which to stand, while the strong neighbour to the north and Chu to the south were in no position to send aid. The third layer is Han's own decay: after King Huanhui the Han court made repeated pledges of land, grain and the profits of the frontier marts to Qin in exchange for loans; the service and the levies shrank year by year, and the garrisons of the counties were reduced to token numbers; and in the reign of King An, private intercourse between the Han court and Qin agents appears again and again in the pages of the historians. Diplomacy offered no way out either: Su Qin surveyed the position of the six states and urged Han to join the vertical alliance, and the king of Han did not take it; Han even tried to use the strength of Qin against Zhao, which in the narrative of the Su Qin biography only handed Qin an additional title and an additional road. The fourth layer is Qin's preparation: the farming-and-war system left by Shang Yang turned the surplus of Guanzhong into grain for campaigns year after year, and the levying of the counties, the relay of the post stations and the building of roads along the route meant that a large army never had to take its grain from the country it marched through; on the armoury side Qin had its own specialised workshops for crossbow mechanisms and arrow shafts, and had taken over the ironworking and crossbow skills of Han and Chu. The Zhengguo Canal was Han's last delaying move, and the result was one more stretch of fields for Qin.
impact: 韓國的滅亡是秦統一工程的起點，而不是終點。前230年之後，趙、魏、楚、燕、齊五國還在，但秦國的滅國機器已經轉動：前228年秦破趙、毀邯鄲，前225年滅魏，前223年滅楚，前222年滅燕與魏，到前221年齊國降秦，十二年間六國盡滅。制度上，韓是第一個被徹底郡縣化的國家——秦沒有像前代那樣分封韓王族，而是把韓地直接置郡，韓故都新鄭一帶劃入潁川郡，部分城池歸入南陽郡；從此中原的關隘要地如宜陽、成皋、陽翟，與洛河谷的通道全部握在秦軍手裡，秦國自洛陽出兵的距離縮短到數日可達。土地與賦役上，韓的編戶齊民被併入秦的郡縣田制，韓地多年累積的冶鐵、弓弩、陶鑄與刻工被秦吸收，兵器上的「工師」銘牌制度正是在這樣的作坊體系裡成熟；韓人也沒有消失，韓非曾以韓國公子的身分入秦，老將鄭國主持的工程留在關中，秦軍的作坊裡也留著韓地匠人的技藝。對六國而言，韓亡帶來的是震懼與兩難：《戰國策》裡那個「唇亡則齒寒」的比喻，講的正是韓、魏一旦失一，另一個就再也擋不住秦的次第推進；秦軍在東方推進得越順，剩下各國能聯手的地方就越少。對後世而言，這場戰爭的真正意義是標示出郡縣制在中原的落地方式：從韓的郡縣被秦接管的那一刻起，戰國的封建秩序就開始被逐步替換成郡縣秩序，最終隨著前221年的統一而成為帝國的骨架。
impactEn: The destruction of Han was the beginning of Qin's unification project, not its end. After 230 BC the five states of Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi still stood, but the machine that was breaking them up was already turning: Qin broke Zhao and destroyed Handan in 228 BC, destroyed Wei in 225, destroyed Chu in 223, destroyed Yan and Wei in 222, and Qi surrendered in 221, so that within twelve years all six were gone. Institutionally, Han was the first state to be thoroughly turned into commanderies and counties. Qin did not, as older practice would have allowed, enfeoff the royal house of Han, but simply created commanderies over Han's land, the old capital at Xinzheng and its neighbourhood passing into the Ying River commandery and some of its towns into the Nanyang commandery; from that moment the passes and key points of the central plain, Yiyang, Chenggao and Yangdi, and the corridor of the Luo valley were all in the hands of the Qin army, and the distance of an army out of Luoyang shrank to a few days. In land and taxation the registered households of Han were folded into the commandery system of Qin, and the ironworking, bow and crossbow making, pottery and engraving of Han territory were absorbed by Qin, whose armoury matured its practice of stamping the name of the responsible master craftsman on the fittings; the people of Han did not vanish either. Han Fei went to Qin as a prince of the Han house, the works begun by the old engineer Zheng Guo remained in Guanzhong, and the skills of Han craftsmen stayed on in the Qin workshops. For the six states, the fall of Han brought terror and a dilemma: the image of the lip and the teeth in the Strategies of the Warring States speaks exactly of Han and Wei, where the loss of one left the other unable to hold back the advance of Qin; the further Qin's armies pushed east, the less room was left for the remaining states to act together. For later ages the real meaning of the war lies in the way it marks the arrival of the commandery system in the central plain: from the moment Han's counties passed into Qin's hands, the feudal order of the Warring States began to be replaced step by step by a system of commanderies, which became the skeleton of the empire with the unification of 221 BC.
result: 結果在一年之內落定。西元前230年，韓王安在節節失守之後遣使向秦請降，秦軍受降，韓國的城邑相繼入秦，成為六國中最先被滅的一個。韓王安被封為通武君，遷居秦地居住，韓國的宗廟與封邑就此中斷；數年後他因子孫謀反被誅，韓氏宗族的政治生命在秦律之下正式終結。土地方面，韓地置郡，新鄭、陽翟、黃池等縣劃入潁川郡，宜陽、陽城一帶的部分地界與南陽郡相連，韓最後的幾座關城成為秦軍的永久前哨。從大戰略看，滅韓解決了三件事：秦國拔掉了六國中最靠近關中、最容易先取的一塊，補上了洛河谷與黃河南岸的通道；中原的縱向聯防從此無從談起，韓與魏之間的唇齒關係也隨韓亡而失效；秦國的軍隊第一次不是在戰場上擊敗一個對手，而是在一個已經失去縱深的國家身上，把遠征、圍城與接管一次做完。這個模式在接下來的十一年裡被反覆複製：前228年滅趙，前225年滅魏，前223年滅楚，前222年滅燕與魏，前221年滅齊，最後由秦始皇在咸陽完成帝號，郡縣、度量衡、書同文與車同軌隨之推向全國。對韓國本身而言，它作為獨立政權的歷史停在西元前230年，但韓的文字風格、兵器技藝與人脈並沒有隨著都城失守而斷絕，反而被秦漢的制度一節一節地接了下去。
resultEn: The result was settled within a single year. In 230 BC, after losing ground in succession, King An of Han sent envoys to Qin to sue for peace; the Qin army accepted the surrender, the cities of Han passed to Qin one after another, and Han became the first of the six states to be destroyed. King An was given the title Lord of Tongwu and resettled in Qin territory, and the ancestral temples and fiefs of Han were cut off there and then; several years later he was put to death with his descendants for conspiracy, and the political life of the Han house came formally to an end under Qin law. On the ground, commanderies were created over Han's territory: Xinzheng, Yangdi and Huangchi passed into the Ying River commandery, while parts of the ground around Yiyang and Yangcheng were joined to the Nanyang commandery, and the last Han passes became permanent outposts of the Qin army. On the greater strategic level the conquest of Han settled three things. Qin removed from the map the piece of the six states that lay nearest to Guanzhong and was easiest to take first, and completed its grip on the corridor of the Luo valley and the southern bank of the Yellow River; the vertical defence of the central plain could no longer be discussed at all, and the lip-and-teeth relationship between Han and Wei lapsed with the fall of Han; and for the first time the Qin army did not defeat an opponent on a field of battle, but finished a distant expedition, a siege and a takeover in one movement against a state that had already lost its depth. The pattern was copied again and again over the next eleven years: Zhao in 228 BC, Wei in 225, Chu in 223, Yan and Wei in 222, Qi in 221, until the First Emperor of Qin took the imperial title at Xianyang, and commanderies, weights and measures, a uniform script and a uniform gauge of the axle were carried out across the country. For Han itself the history of the state as an independent power ends in 230 BC, but the character of Han writing, the craft of Han arms and the ties of Han people did not break with the loss of the capital; they were taken up link by link by the institutions of Qin and Han.
